source.title: Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles II: Examples, Applications and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For each integer d at least 2, does there exist a family of finite d-dimensional bounded-degree topological expanders, meaning simplicial complexes of dimension d whose vertex degrees are uniformly bounded and that satisfy Gromov's topological overlapping property?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.2. For d ≥ 2, are there families of d-dimensional bounded degree topological expanders?
Problem 1.2 was resolved in full — first for d = 2 in [KKL16], and later for all dimensions in [EK16] — without resolving Problem 1.3.

accepted.question_text: For each integer d at least 3, does there exist a family of finite d-dimensional bounded-degree simplicial complexes whose i-coboundary Cheeger constants with F2 coefficients are uniformly bounded away from zero, i.e. a family of d-dimensional bounded-degree F2-coboundary expanders?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.3. For d ≥ 2, are there families of d-dimensional bounded degree F2-coboundary expanders?
In Section 5, we provide a solution to Problem 1.3 for the d = 2 case (it remains open for d ≥ 3).

accepted.question_text: Let G be a simple p-adic Lie group of rank d at least 3, let B be the associated Bruhat-Tits building, and assume p is sufficiently large depending on d. For every lattice Γ of G, is the quotient complex Γ\B a 1-cocycle expander with permutation coefficients, i.e. does h1(Γ\B, Sym) stay positive?
accepted.context_brief: p-adic lattices and permutation cocycle expansion

evidence.quote:
Conjecture 6.1. Let G be simple p-adic Lie group of rank d ≥ 3, and p ≥ p(d) ≫ 0. Then, for any lattice Γ of G,
(6.1) h1(Γ\B , Sym) > 0,
where B is the Bruat–Tits building associated with G.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a finitely presented group that is not sofic, meaning a group for which no sequence of maps into symmetric groups simultaneously makes every defining relation asymptotically hold in normalized Hamming distance while keeping every nontrivial word uniformly far from the identity permutation?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.3 (Gromov [Gro99], Weiss [Wei00]). Are there non-sofic groups?

Definition 6.2. A finitely presented group Γ ∼= hS|Ri is said to be sofic if there is a sequence of functions fn : S → Sym(n), such that
∀r ∈ R : dh(fn(r),Id) n→∞ −−−→ 0,
and for every w /∈ hhRii,
lim inf(dh(fn(w),Id)) ≥ 1/2.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an infinite family of connected finite polygonal complexes {Xm} whose vertex degrees are uniformly bounded and for which both the 0-dimensional and 1-dimensional coboundary Cheeger constants with permutation coefficients are bounded below by the same positive constant λ, that is, h0^B(Xm, Sym) and h1^B(Xm, Sym) are at least λ for all m?

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.5 (Bounded coboundary expanders in permutations). Is there such a family for which
∀m ∈ N : hB0(Xm, Sym), hB1(Xm, Sym) ≥ λ,
for some λ > 0 independent of m?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an infinite family of connected finite polygonal complexes {Xm} whose vertex degrees are uniformly bounded and for which the 0-dimensional and 1-dimensional cocycle Cheeger constants with permutation coefficients, together with the first cosystole with permutation coefficients, are all bounded below by the same positive constant λ, that is, h0(Xm, Sym), h1(Xm, Sym), and CoSyst1(Xm, Sym) are at least λ for all m?
accepted.context_brief: bounded cocycle expanders with large cosystoles

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.6 (Bounded cocycle expanders with large cosystoles in permutations). Is there such a family for
which
∀m ∈ N : h0(Xm, Sym), h1(Xm, Sym), CoSyst1(Xm, Sym) ≥ λ,
where λ > 0 is independent of m?

accepted.question_text: For random simplicial complexes or random group presentations, what is the expected homomorphism or cocycle stability rate, especially in the mid-range where positive stability would have consequences for the existence of non-sofic groups and for residual finiteness of hyperbolic groups?
accepted.context_brief: random models and expected stability rate

evidence.quote: It is natural to ask what is the expected stability rate of a random object.

In that paper, it is proved that if the expected cocycle Cheeger constant with permutation coefficients of a random simplicial complex in the mid-range is bounded away from zero, then there are non-sofic hyperbolic groups.

accepted.question_text: For the finite simple groups SL_n(F_p) and related groups of Lie type, is there a uniform positive lower bound on the cocycle Cheeger constants in permutations for the Steinberg presentations, at least when n is fixed and p tends to infinity, while the cocycle Cheeger constants for the short Guralnick-Kantor-Kassabov-Lubotzky presentations tend to zero when either n or p tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.7. There is a uniform lower bound on the cocycle Cheeger constant in permutations of the Steinberg presentations, at least when fixing n and tending p to ∞. On the contrary, the cocycle Cheeger constants in permutations of the GKKL presentations tend to zero when either n or p tending to ∞.

accepted.question_text: Find a family of finite groups G with presentations G ≅ <S|R> such that the presentations are short in the sense that the numbers of generators and relations are polylogarithmic in |G| and every relation has polylogarithmic length in |G|, while the stability rate is still strong enough that the presentation is ρ-stable with ρ(ε) = polyloglog(|G|) · ε^c for some constant c > 0 independent of |G|.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.9 (Efficient stability in permutations). Find a family of finite groups {G}, with presentations
G ∼= hS|Ri, such that:
• The presentation is (somewhat) short:
|S|, |R| = polylog(|G|)
∀r ∈ R : |r| = polylog(|G|).
• The stability rate is good: hS|Ri is ρ-stable, and ρ(ε) = polyloglog(|G|) · εc for some c > 0 independent
of |G|.

accepted.question_text: Given a binary linear code Ker(A) defined by a matrix A and the associated presentation of F2^k generated by involution, commutation, and linear relations coming from A, what can be proved about the homomorphism stability rate of this presentation when the test maps are allowed to take values in arbitrary symmetric groups Sym(n), rather than being restricted to Sym(2)? In particular, what happens for presentations coming from Reed-Muller codes or from recently constructed good locally testable codes?
accepted.context_brief: locally testable codes with permutation coefficients

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.11 (Locally testable codes with permutation coefficients). Given a matrix A ∈ Mm×n(F2), one can
define the following presentation of Fk2, where k = n − rank(A):

What about the case where the inputs are not restricted to be with range Sym(2), but any Sym(n)? Namely, what can be said about the homomorphism stability rate of the above presentation for a given code? For the Hadamard code the resulting presentation is essentially the multiplication table of Fk2, and is thus stable but expansive. What about more reasonably sized codes, such as Reed–Muller codes? Or, the recently constructed good locally testable codes [DEL+22,PK22]?

accepted.question_text: Does the metric quotient U(n)/Sym(n), where U(n) carries the relevant unitary metric and Sym(n) is embedded as permutation matrices, satisfy a Poincare-type inequality with constants independent of n?

evidence.quote: it would be useful to have a Poincare-type inequality (cf. Lemma 5.4 in [CL23]) on the metric space U(n)/Sym(n), with constants independent of n.
But, the case of U(n)/Sym(n) seems to be open, and will be sufficient for us to translate the results of [JNV+22] to the permutation setup.

Extracted Problem 6.5 verbatim and rewrote it into a standalone bounded-family question.
Extracted Problem 6.6 verbatim and preserved all three required lower bounds in the rewrite.
Accepted the random-models question because the section explicitly asks for the expected stability rate of a random object and ties it to concrete downstream open problems.
Extracted Conjecture 6.7 on Steinberg versus GKKL presentations.
Extracted Problem 6.9 and retained the short-presentation and stability-rate requirements.
Extracted Problem 6.11 and expanded the question using only the in-source description of the presentation and the explicit follow-up about Sym(n) inputs.
Accepted the final open metric-geometry question because the paper explicitly says the U(n)/Sym(n) case seems open.
Kept the introduction problems and later Section 6 problems as separate items because they ask materially different questions.
